//: Statements of the certified item that ARMv7-A's coverage suite does not
reach, each with the reason no run on the measured machine can. Read by
scripts/gen-coverage-justification.py, which files each line in the
category named here instead of its file's, and fails when a line named
is no longer in coverage-residual-armv7a.json (a test reaches it now, or
it moved) or when `match` is not on the first line named. Line numbers
are the tree's the residual was measured on: main 2f38c82a and branch
cov-d-arm. Written 2026-09-26 for F-10: the architecture's own code
(arch/armv7a and ARMv7-A's share of arch); the generic modules' residual
on this architecture is not argued here.

arguments.why: The end of `write_byte`, to which this build attributes the jump out of its arm for ST's USART, the STM32MP157's console. QEMU's `virt` has a PL011; the USART is the DK1 board's, whose driver `arch/stm32_usart.rs` is argued as that board's as a whole. Which port a tree makes the console is held by the stage 3 machine check to four trees, one an STM32MP15's; the board boots on this port (docs/vendor/st/stm32mp157-dk.md, "What is actually verified").
Mapping ST's USART, the STM32MP157's console, when the device tree names one. A command typed at busybox's prompt ran on the board (docs/vendor/st/stm32mp157-dk.md, "What is actually verified").

PSCI `SYSTEM_OFF` or `SYSTEM_RESET` through the secure monitor. QEMU's `virt` without EL3 firmware answers PSCI itself through `hvc`, and its tree says so; the DK1's TF-A and OP-TEE answer through `smc`, and the board powers off and resets through this call (`ferrix.onexit=reset` resets the board to U-Boot, docs/vendor/st/stm32mp157-dk.md, "What is actually verified").

A PSCI call through the secure monitor, `CPU_ON` for a secondary. As line 181: QEMU answers by `hvc`; the DK1's secure firmware by `smc`, through which the board starts its second processor (`2 online`, docs/vendor/st/stm32mp157-dk.md, "What is actually verified").

A page address past 4 GiB asked to be invalidated, which on this architecture cannot be a translation; everything is flushed rather than a truncated page. Every caller passes a virtual address, all of which are below 4 GiB here.

Firmware whose PSCI `SYSTEM_RESET` returned instead of resetting: the machine is powered off rather than carrying on as though it had reset. The suite's `boot-reset` gate takes the reset, and QEMU and the DK1 both reset.

arguments.match: return Err("this GIC is not a GICv2, and GICv3 support is not written yet");
arguments.why: A device tree describing a GICv3 on ARMv7-A, which this kernel has no driver for here: interrupt bring-up is refused by name and the kernel stops (FX-0303). The machines it runs on -- QEMU's `virt` as the suite boots it, the STM32MP157 -- have a GICv2; a `virt` given a GICv3 would be a boot that stops, which is not coverage evidence.

`nosmp`, read on this architecture from `/chosen/bootargs` as U-Boot's `bootargs` sets it (docs/vendor/st/stm32mp157-dk.md: `setenv bootargs 'nosmp'`). QEMU's U-Boot passes no bootargs and the suite cannot give it any; the loader's command line, which the suite can write, is not where this architecture looks. AArch64 reads it from the loader, and its suite boots it (`boot-nosmp`).

A processor node with no `enable-method`, taken to mean PSCI where the tree has a `/psci` node, as Linux does on this architecture. QEMU's tree names `psci` on every processor; the STM32MP157's `/cpus` nodes carry none, and the DK1 starts both processors through this rule (`2 online`, docs/vendor/st/stm32mp157-dk.md, "What is actually verified").

`ACTLR.SMP` set on some processors and clear on others: firmware that joined some cores to coherency and missed the rest, which the boot reports rather than proceeds silently on. QEMU reports it clear on every processor, which the suite's boots print (`ACTLR.SMP clear on all 2 processors`).

The speculation check holds each part to its barrier through `Part::barrier`, running this arm in the copy the check inlines under another row. The line's only statement row is in `init`'s copy, which takes it on a Cortex-A9, A12 or A17: none of them runs on QEMU's `virt`, which needs the generic timer the A9 lacks.
As line 73, for the Cortex-A8: run by the speculation check under another row; `init`'s copy takes it only on an A8, which QEMU's `virt` cannot run.

The row is `save_user_state`'s return with no VFP registers to save (`user_fpu_doubles` zero): a core without VFP. Every ARMv7-A core the kernel boots on -- QEMU's Cortex-A7 and A15, the STM32MP157's A7 -- has VFP with 32 double registers, and the save path runs on every switch.

Run by `object/check.rs`'s null write, which ends its program with SIGSEGV and `SEGV_MAPERR`, through the copy of `fault_signal` that `handle_page_fault` inlines, under another row. The line's only statement row is in the copy `dispatch` inlines through `user_fault` for traps that are not page faults, where a page fault cannot arrive.

`classify`'s arm for a vector entry that is neither an interrupt, an undefined instruction, a system call nor an abort: reset, hypervisor trap or FIQ. The stage 3 machine check classifies each from a built frame, in its own copy under other rows; the line's only statement row is in `dispatch`'s copy, which none of those entries reaches on a running kernel -- the stubs for them are the kernel's own failure, which it stops on.

`abort`'s arm for a fault status that is neither translation, access flag, permission, alignment nor debug: an external abort. The stage 3 machine check decodes data and prefetch external aborts from built frames, in its own copy; the line's only statement row is in `dispatch`'s copy, which runs it only when the memory system reports an external abort, which QEMU's does not.
The register dump the trap path prints when the kernel stops on an exception it cannot handle (`trap::report`), and `kind_name` as it inlines it there; a passing run never prints it.
`kind_name` for the reset entry, in `classify`'s arm above (line 550): named by the machine check's frame in its own copy, and in `dispatch`'s only when the kernel's reset stub is taken.
`kind_name` for the hypervisor-trap entry, as line 592.

`disable`'s bit, run by the stage 3 machine check, which masks an idle shared line and an idle private one and reads each back, in the copy it inlines under another row. The line's only statement rows are in the copies `device::Vector::set_masked` and `object::interrupt::take_delivery` inline, for a line masked at the controller because a driver holds it; this machine's device vectors are MSI-X vectors.

A `GICv2m` frame whose SPI range firmware states. ACPI's MADT does, and AArch64 reaches this line on every boot; a device tree may with `arm,msi-base-spi`, and QEMU's for ARMv7-A does not, so the range is read from the frame's own register instead (the arm below it).

The stage 3 machine check reads the doorbell and requires a page, in its own copy under another row. The line's only statement row is in the copy the IOMMU's SMMUv3 bring-up inlines, to map the doorbell into a translated domain; ARMv7-A brings up no SMMUv3 (U-Boot keeps its devices from offering translation).

arguments.match: return Err("the machine describes no usable GICv2m frame");
arguments.why: A vector asked of a GICv2 without a `GICv2m` frame. QEMU's `virt` gives every GICv2 one; the STM32MP157's GIC has none, and its devices interrupt by line.

arguments.match: return Err("every GICv2m SPI is allocated");
arguments.why: Every one of the frame's SPIs taken, up to 64. The machine's devices take one each, five at most, and a vector is never given back while its device runs; a machine with more message-signalled vectors than the frame has SPIs would reach it.

The row is the retry after a lost compare-exchange: another processor took an SPI between this one's read of the bitmap and its claim. Vectors are taken while device nodes are brought up and drivers started, one at a time, so no allocation races another; the loop keeps the bitmap right if one ever does.

The wait for room in the transmit FIFO taking a second turn. QEMU's PL011 model sends each byte as it is written and never reports `FR.TXFF`; a real PL011 at 115200 baud fills its sixteen-byte FIFO in 1.4 ms of output. The DK1's console is ST's USART, not a PL011.

The drain's second turn: the port still sending. QEMU's PL011 reports its FIFO empty and not busy at every read; the loop exists for a real port, whose last line would otherwise be cut off by the power-off.

A received byte carrying a framing, parity, break or overrun flag. QEMU's PL011 flags a byte only for a break on its character device, which no gate sends; on a real port it is line noise. The byte is delivered either way.

`none` names an empty set of defences, which only a `--mitigations off` build records: on ARMv7-A every processor's plan in the certified build holds the index clamp, a Cortex-A7's as well (`speculation defences: clamped indices`). That build is another configuration, not the one certified.

The head of the host region in front of the per-frame array. `BootView::page_array_host` places the array at the front of the usable region it chooses, so on every machine the region has a tail after the array and no head before it; the branch keeps a later placement policy from silently losing the head. `disown_frame`'s only caller is `object::pin`'s quarantine. ARMv7-A's kernel programs no IOMMU unit, by design: `bring_up_smmu` reads only the IORT, which ARMv7-A's firmware does not provide, and the SMMUv3 its `virt` describes is left alone, since U-Boot keeps its virtio devices from offering the platform's translation. Every device domain there is untranslated, and a pin's quarantine exists only for a translated domain (`Pin::map`, `Pin::drop`): the quarantine and its release are x86-64's and AArch64's code, compiled into ARMv7-A's kernel and never asked there. The pin budget's checks (`check_budget`) return at their first line on ARMv7-A, as they say they do with no translated domain.

The statement runs in every kernel unmap, and its refusal runs too: the allocation sweep's `stacks` scenario (`user/alloc_check.rs`) frees two stacks under one shootdown, whose table reservation spills past the eight inline slots, and on the run that fails that reservation the unmap goes on in pieces (seen with a print on the branch, `8 12`, and in `unmap_kernel_in_pieces`'s rows, which are reached). The line's only statement rows are on the other way the reservation fails -- the heap refusing after the injection let it through, which needs the size class out of slab pages at that moment -- inside the inlined `try_reserve`.

The return of a piece the kernel's tables refused to unmap. `unmap_range` refuses only a range that is not page aligned or that would cut a block mapping in half, and the arena maps every stack and buffer page by page at page-aligned addresses, so no piece is refused; the row on this build is that error's way out of the function.

The interrupt controller refused to unmask a line it had just registered a handler for. A vector is minted by its device node only for a line the controller can route (`device::DeviceNode::vector`), and unmasking one is a register write the controller does not refuse; the branch unclaims the line so a controller that did refuse would not leave it claimed.

The root job is made once, by bring-up, before any program exists to be told memory ran out; the allocation is FATAL-ALLOC by design (`tools/common/check/check-fallible-alloc.py` lists it) and this is the panic it ends in. A run reaching it is a boot that ran out of memory before its first program.

`Pin::new` fills both fields, and only this `drop` takes them, once; they are `Option`s so that the drop can move them out. The `else` is the pattern's other half, reached only if a pin were dropped twice.

A packet that found no room. The queue's capacity is kept at PORT_CAPACITY plus every registration's and binding's promised packet (`Promise::new` reserves before a registration is accepted), so a packet either kind of limit allows always fits; the count is what would show the accounting broken.

A packet taken by a wait whose buffer faulted, put back when the queue is at capacity and cannot grow. Its slot is taken meanwhile only if a user packet was queued between the take and the put-back, and then the reserve must also fail; the object edge check puts packets back into a queue with room (`object/edge_check.rs`). The line after the loss is its return.

A fired registration that did not fit on its object's firing list. `register` reserves room on `firing` for every listed registration as each is listed, so moving one there never allocates and cannot fail; the arm keeps the registration listed rather than lose it if that accounting ever broke. The arm's last rows are its jump back into the loop.

The failure half of a debug assertion that interrupts are enabled when a process's watchers are reached: their lock is a plain one, which an interrupt handler may not take. Every caller is a system call or a task's exit, with interrupts on; reaching the row is the assertion firing.
As `Exit::observe`'s: the failure half of the assertion that interrupts are on when a process's watchers are closed.

The failure half of the assertion that an unstarted process's last handle is dropped with interrupts on, since the kill it causes may block. Handles close from system calls and exits, with interrupts on; the object check closes unstarted children's handles and reaches the kill.

The closing row of new_idle_task is the error path's: no memory for a processor's idle task, made once per processor at bring-up with the heap all but empty. The stack is freed and the bring-up fails.

The debug assertion's own row is its panic call: a prepared task dropped with interrupts masked, which would free its stack waiting on every processor with interrupts off. The condition is evaluated under line 1105's and 1113's rows, which are reached (an unstarted child's drop at stage 9).

After the switch away from a dead task, which never returns to it: a dead task is never picked again (stage 5's a_dead_task_is_not_filed_as_a_sleeper, and check_invariants' DEAD_STILL_QUEUED, hold that). If it ever were picked, halting here is the only answer that corrupts nothing.

FX-0503: a task blocked or yielded while holding a lock that disables preemption, which the preemption count cannot survive. The report names the lock's site and stops the machine; a kernel that never blocks under a spin lock never takes it.

The times of a queue whose processor has not joined the scheduler: only between sched::init and a secondary's arrival, before any program can read /proc/stat, or on a machine where a processor failed to start, which stage 4 refuses.

A task queued without its run slot, or refused by the fair class: the slot is missing only if the task is already queued, which every caller's is_queued check rules out, and the fair class refuses only a duplicate identifier or a zero weight, neither of which the kernel makes. Counted (MISSING_SLOTS) and required zero by check_invariants.

Run by every wait on a queue. In the ARMv7-A image the loop's head keeps a row only in the render core's monomorph, which ARMv7-A's virt, with no render device, never calls; the others carry it under the first statement's row.

Run by stage 5's sched::check::before_start, which waits on two queues before the scheduler starts and requires the wait to last until its deadline. In that monomorph the ready closure is `|| false`, folded into the loop, and the spin carries no row of its own; this line's rows are in monomorphs whose waits all run with the scheduler up.
The debug assertion's own row is its panic call: a sleeping lock taken where a task may not block. The condition runs on every sleeping-lock acquisition under another row.

The wait's exit test on a kernel with no personality registered: every build registers one before the first program runs (register_load, checked at boot), so a native wait always asks the personality.

Run by stage 9's object check, which duplicates a handle asking for rights it does not hold and requires ACCESS_DENIED. On AArch64 every caller that meets AccessDenied inlines table_error; the arm's row is only in the out-of-line copy.

Run by the native refusal check: a duplicate into a full table answers NO_HANDLES and a message naming one handle twice answers INVALID_ARGS, both required. Those callers inline table_error; the arms' rows are only in its out-of-line copy, whose callers never meet these two errors.
The queue refusing to take back at its head a message it gave up a moment earlier: its capacity still holds the slot, so putting it back needs no memory.
The closing row of image_bytes is the drop of its buffer when a page of the image's VMO cannot be read: a VMO's pages up to its length always read, a decommitted one as zeros.

A child whose table closed between the start's claim and the move -- killed in that window -- or one with no room: a child that has not run has an empty table with a limit of 4096, and a kill in the window is a race no check can place.

An insert into the target table that fails although room was checked and reserved under the same lock a statement earlier: the object is put back in the source, or freed if even that fails. The handle table's insert refuses only without room or memory, and both were settled under the held lock.

A coherent pin for a device that does not snoop the caches: the STM32MP15's peripherals. Every device QEMU presents is DMA-coherent (PCI on q35, and dma-coherent virtio-mmio on virt), so past_caches is false on every measured machine.

`ferrix_vma::AddressSpace::new` refuses a window whose ends are not page aligned or out of order, and the window here is `MMAP_MIN_ADDR..USER_VIRT_END`, two constants of the layout that are both. Reported rather than panicked on, as the comment says.

A page found held by a device between the fault reading its reference count and taking it. A pin makes a shared page the object's own first (`Vmo::hold` copies it), so a copy-on-write fault finds a held page only if a pin lands in those few instructions on another processor, which no check can place deterministically.

The region `resolve` found to be a private file mapping is gone, or is no longer one, when this takes the space's lock again: `resolve` lets the lock go to call here. Reached only if another thread of the process unmaps or replaces the region in that gap, while this one faults on it; the fault then answers as for an address with nothing mapped, which is what it has become.

A private file mapping's region whose file object or shadow is missing from the tables. `map_file` records both under the region's id before the region can fault, and they leave together as the region's id leaves; a fault finding one missing would be the tables and the map disagreeing.

The failure half of the debug assertion that a user page fault is resolved with no preemption-disabling lock held (a fault may sleep for a page from a disk). Every fault path takes its locks inside the resolution, after this; reaching the row is the assertion firing.

The failure half of the debug assertion that a user page fault is resolved with no preemption-disabling lock held (a fault may sleep for a page from a disk). Every fault path takes its locks inside the resolution, after this; reaching the row is the assertion firing.

`map_anywhere`'s refusal of a place outside the user half. `find_free` answers only places inside the map's window, `MMAP_MIN_ADDR..USER_VIRT_END`, so the place it found is always inside the half; the check keeps the rule where the mapping is made rather than in the map's contract.

`map_shared_code`'s refusal of a place outside the user half, as `map_anywhere`'s is. `find_free` answers only places inside the map's window (its contract, `src/lib/kernel/vma/src/lib.rs`), and a space's window is `MMAP_MIN_ADDR..USER_VIRT_END` when built (`AddressSpace::new`) and never raised past `USER_VIRT_END` after (`set_ceiling` refuses it), so the place found is always inside the half; the check keeps the rule where the mapping is made rather than in the map's contract.

A page already held four billion times, whose count would wrap. Each hold is a pin a driver made and keeps a handle to, and a process may hold at most HANDLE_LIMIT (4,096) handles, so the count cannot approach the limit; the refusal is what keeps a wrapped count from freeing a page a device still reaches.

A span given back from the middle of a merged region, which splits it, when the arena's region list is full and the heap has nothing to grow it with. The split reserves with the standard library's `try_reserve` (libs/vma `remove_quietly`), which the failure injection deliberately does not fail -- with room in the list it allocates nothing -- so reaching it needs the list at its capacity at the moment the heap is out of pages; the span then stays reserved, address space lost rather than memory, and is counted.

The arena's map refusing to give back a span for a reason other than memory: `OutOfRange`, a span outside the arena's window. Every span came from `reserve`, which found it inside the window, so none is. The closing rows are the error arms' return.

`map_device`'s window could not be mapped after its span was reserved: the kernel's tables refused, for a table they could not have or a block in the way. Device windows are mapped once each at bring-up, when memory is plentiful, into an arena no block mapping covers.
`check_failed_device_map`, stage 2's own check, could not map the page it needs as an obstacle, and fails the boot. A passing run never takes it.

A device window among the stacks being freed. Stacks are made only by `allocate_stack`, as anonymous memory, and callers free only stacks they made; the arm frees such a window without giving its frames to the buddy allocator, since they are a device's.

The Interrupt arm of `Trap`'s derived Debug. The only formatting of a `Trap` is the `signal ... ended by signal` line in `user_fault_as`, whose trap comes from `user_fault` or `handle_page_fault`; `dispatch` sends every Interrupt to the controller and never there. Reaching this would mean the dispatcher had treated a device interrupt as a program's fault.

The stop when the architecture refuses a system call trap. On this architecture `system_call` (arch/armv7a/trap.rs) refuses only an `svc` taken from SVC mode, and the kernel issues no `svc` of its own: every `svc` in the tree is in a program's bytes.

An undefined instruction or an unexpected exception taken in the kernel, which stops it. The same exceptions from a program are reached, by the trap check's programs (arch/armv7a/trap/check.rs), through the arm above these.

A system call with no dispatcher registered. `main.rs` registers the item's dispatcher before anything can enter user mode, and the first registration stands, so in this item every call finds one. The arm is what the core answers when built without a dispatcher above it, rather than a panic in a trap vector.
A fault from user mode with no personality registered, which the kernel stops on; `main.rs` registers the Linux personality's return path before the first program.
A fault from user mode that the personality finds no process for, which the kernel stops on: every task that enters ring 3 is a process's thread.

A fault from user mode on a task with no address space. `sched` gives a task made for a thread its process's space before it first runs, so this would be the kernel having entered ring 3 without recording who was running; it is reported as fatal rather than resolved.
The report of a page fault the kernel could not resolve -- one in the kernel outside the demand window, or a user one with no program to blame -- printed as the kernel stops.
`fatal` and `report`, the trap path's stop: the architecture's register dump, the abridged report for a second failure, and the panic's conclusion. Reached only when the kernel stops on a trap.

The release's add-back: a release found the count, or for a lock the locks held, already zero, so the word is put back before unmatched() stops the machine with SCHEDULE_WITH_PREEMPTION_HELD (FX-0503). A kernel that releases every lock on the processor that took it never takes it. Shown reached by the negative controls on 3bb22d1bf, logs in ~/.local/share/ferrix/logs/step2a/: 2b-ctl-unmatched-enable (a release with nothing raised) and the three atomicity controls 2b-ctl-x86-address-then-add, 2b-ctl-arm-unmasked-a64 and 2b-ctl-arm-unmasked-a32-smp2, each of which reached this path and stopped the boot on FX-0503's message.

unmatched(), carried from sched/mod.rs 257-258 where the same arm stood before 2b: a lock taken on one processor was released on another, or a release had nothing to lower. It names where the count was last raised and stops the machine with SCHEDULE_WITH_PREEMPTION_HELD; a kernel that releases every lock where it took it never takes it. preempt_site, carried from sched/mod.rs 266: where a processor's count was last raised, read only by the two failure reports that name it (unmatched(), and schedule_from's switch with the count raised); neither runs in a passing boot.
